conviction_note: Linc is an investment company whose Q3 NAV is roughly 90% computable from public prices (listed holdings 64% of NAV, US healthcare ETF insurance wrapper ~19%), so the print carries little new on the number; the two small positive findings rest on the share's discount having widened from 3-10% (Mar-Aug month-ends) to an estimated ~16-17% once the buyback bid stopped on 21 Sept, which the report's NAV re-anchors and a renewed buyback would address; both are inference, so p_up sits at 55 on an abs move of 3.5 and the scaled number (+0.35) is well below the findings' sum (+1.2) because the sign is barely better than a coin.

findings.finding: The share has fallen from 71.1 SEK on 21 Sept (the last buyback day) to 67.6, while my reconstruction of NAV from public prices is roughly flat to up (about 79.5-80 at 30 Sept, about 81 now), so the discount to NAV has widened to an estimated ~16-17% against 3.4%, 8.7%, 5.5% and 10.4% at the March, June, July and August month-ends; the report puts an official NAV beside the price and on two of the last two quarters the report day moved the price toward the published NAV (Q1: stock at a premium fell 9.3%; Q2: +3.2%).

findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: every input is public, so a reader who rebuilds the NAV sees the discount today. What is not in the price is an official figure: the September NAV was not published as a monthly release (the Q3 report replaces it), the name has one analyst (ABGSC) and $0.23m a day of turnover, and the discount widened while the only steady buyer (the company, 7-8k shares a day against 25-50k traded) was absent. If the market were holding the NAV in view, the discount would not have moved six points in a month in which the NAV barely moved. Inference, not a sourced estimate, so sized small.
findings.independence: The month-end prices behind the discount history and the holdings' moves come from a different source (Yahoo bars, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/LINC.ST?range=2y&interval=1d); the H1 report's NAV of 77.9 at 30 June (https://storage.mfn.se/50812a97-990b-4967-b03d-ced877a86ac5/2026-q2-delarsrapport-linc-ab-vfinal.pdf) anchors the q/q comparison. Shares the buyback timeline with the second finding.

findings.finding: The first buyback programme expired on 30 Sept at 311,436 of the 650,000 shares intended, with no purchases reported after 21 Sept (the start of the 30-day closed period before this report); the AGM 2026 mandate allows holdings of own shares up to 10%, so the report day is the first open window in which the board could restart the bid that had been 15-25% of daily volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: One prior instance: the programme was announced 2026-05-21 at 23:30; the share closed 73.1 on 22 May against 72.5-73 in the days before (Yahoo bars), so the announcement itself moved the price under 1%; the support showed up as a discount that stayed at 5-10% while it ran and widened once it stopped.

Återköpsprogrammet löper från den 21 maj 2026 och fram till 30 september 2026 (Total under the programme 311,436 shares, SEK 22,798,835 ... The programme runs from 21 May 2026 until 30 September 2026); and from https://mfn.se/a/linc-ab/linc-beslutar-om-aktieaterkopsprogram: 'Det totala antalet aktier som får återköpas ska begränsas så att Lincs innehav av egna aktier vid var tid inte överstiger 10 procent ... Bolagets avsikt är att återköpa maximalt 650 000 aktier.'
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing says the board will restart, so the market cannot price a decision that has not been signalled; if it were expecting one, the discount would not have widened since 21 Sept. Unsourced intent, so sized small and with a floor at zero (no new programme is the status quo the price already reflects).
findings.independence: Nasdaq Nordic disclosure feed shows no 'Förändringar i återköpta aktier' release from Linc after 2026-09-21 (https://api.news.eu.nasdaq.com/news/query.action?type=json&freeText=Linc&globalName=NordicAllMarkets&limit=30). Shares the discount reading with the first finding, so the two are not fully independent.
